title: Her only visit to the Plantation; grandmother's reaction
summary: Jelly took her once to hear Bigard and Nicholas with King Oliver; she never saw his nightlife.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I was going to say, do you remember where he worked or what he did when he played? Or did you ever hear him on the job anyplace? No. He never, no.

He never took me out to a nightlife. The only place he took me to one time is because I, Bonnie Bigard and Albert Nicholas worked with King Oliver. At the plantation. And he took me to the plantation so I could hear them. And I mean, I wasn't there an hour, I don't believe, because he said, my eyes were big as soft as looking around. I had never seen the cabaret before.
So your grandmother wouldn't have approved at all. Oh my goodness, no.

And I mean, the funny thing about it, you try to tell your people the truth, you know what I mean? And my grandmother said, well, you evasive. Something's wrong. You know something that you're not telling me. And here it all came out. I would tell everything.
